title: GPU OOM debugging notes (CUDA driver/library mismatch suspect)
content:
Notes/brain dump while reproducing/diagnosing a hard GPU OOM that sometimes correlates with driver/library mismatches. Mostly for myself and for handing off to SRE/infra later.

Summary of the problem:
- Job: large LLM batch inference (seq_len=2048, batch=8, 16-bit) using PyTorch 2.2 wheel built for CUDA 12.1.
- Symptoms: intermittent full-GPU OOM in production container (OOM during KV cache allocation / first forward). Host-level errors sometimes show driver complaints.
- Behavior: restarting the container sometimes resolves the job for a few runs, then OOM returns. Rebooting the node fixes for longer.

Commands & outputs collected (raw):
1) nvidia-smi (on host right after OOM)
$ nvidia-smi -q -d DRIVER
Thu Feb  6 12:07:18 2026
Driver Version: 535.86.01
CUDA Version: 12.2
GPU 0: A100-SXM4-40GB
FB Memory Usage
    Total                       : 40536 MiB
    Used                        : 39980 MiB
    Free                        : 556 MiB

2) dmesg excerpt (around OOM time)
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00.0: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x27: DRM, 0x00000004)
[ 12345.678904] NVRM: The NVIDIA probe routine failed for 0000:3b:00.0.
[ 12345.678906] nvidia-nvlink: NVML library not found

3) container python exception (from task logs)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/inference/worker.py", line 312, in run
    outputs = model.generate(input_ids, max_new_tokens=512)
  File "/opt/conda/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1614, in __call__
    return forward_call(*input, **kwargs)
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 32.00 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 37.12 GiB already allocated; 1.88 GiB free; 36.75 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)

4) python quick checks inside container (post-OOM)
$ python -c "import torch,sys; print(torch.version.cuda); print(torch.cuda.is_available()); print(torch.cuda.device_count()); print(torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)); print(torch.cuda.memory_summary())"
12.1
True
1
NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB
RAM Summary: ... (shows ~37GB allocated/reserved)

5) ldconfig / ldd checks (container)
$ ldd /opt/conda/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/lib/libc10_cuda.so | grep cuda
    libcudart.so.12.1 => /usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64/libcudart.so.12.1 (0x00007f...)
    libcudnn.so.8 => not found

6) host libs
$ ls -l /usr/local/cuda/lib64
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root 22 Jul 23  2025 /usr/local/cuda -> /usr/local/cuda-12.2
$ ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcudart.so.*
/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcudart.so.12.2

Observations so far (hypotheses):
- Mismatch between CUDA reported in container (torch reports 12.1) and host driver CUDA (nvidia-smi: 12.2). PyTorch wheel linked to libcudart 12.1, but host has 12.2 runtime. Normally minor CUDA minor version differences are OK, but the driver/kernel combo (535 driver) might be inconsistent with the modules loaded. dmesg shows 'probe routine failed' and 'NVML library not found' which is suspicious.
- ldd shows libcudnn.so.8 missing in container => falling back to host-installed libraries via LD_LIBRARY_PATH or /usr/local/cuda symlink could produce ABI mismatches.
- Memory numbers: huge reserved block by PyTorch (36.75 GiB) leaving too little for model+kv allocation. Could be memory fragmentation / caching plus driver misreporting.
- Reboots fixing for a while suggests driver module state or persistent GPU state (or memory not being freed at kernel level due to stale processes / nv-peer memory).

Steps/troubleshooting done (and results):
- Restarted only container: sometimes mitigates for 1-3 runs (suggests memory cache in process accounted for).
- Rebooted host: longer fix.
- Verified container uses nvidia runtime (nvidia-container-toolkit) and mounts /usr/local/cuda from host via symlink; found symlink points to 12.2 while torch wants 12.1 -> potential ld path mixing.
- Reinstalled nvidia-driver 535.86.01 via apt on host (idempotent) -> no change.
- Pulled app image built with torch+cua 12.1 -> same OOM.
- Tested small batch sizes (batch=1) -> runs fine (so memory proportional to batch, but OOM threshold changes unpredictably).

Immediate hypotheses prioritized:
1) Host driver/ABI mismatch: although driver reports CUDA 12.2 capability, some kernel modules may be inconsistent (dmesg probe failed). The NVML missing message indicates nvidia libraries not being found inside container or across version mismatch.
2) Container image is mixing host-provided CUDA libraries via /usr/local/cuda symlink -> leads to torch using 12.1 libs but host offers 12.2 binaries -> edge-case ABI incompatibility causing larger-than-expected allocation/reserve.
3) Memory fragmentation / persistent allocations from previous processes (maybe leftover MIG or NVPeer residual) leading to less available contiguous memory for large KV cache allocation.
4) PyTorch+custom CUDA kernels compiled against different ABI (e.g. cuBLAS/cuDNN mismatch) causing unexpected allocation behavior.

Immediate next steps to validate/mitigate (ordered):
- Reproduce on a dedicated test node (non-prod) with the exact container image. Try: reboot node -> start container -> run job repeatedly to see stability window. Log dmesg between runs.
- On test node, ensure container uses only container-provided CUDA libs (unset LD_LIBRARY_PATH to host /usr/local/cuda) and verify ldd points to container libs (libcudart.so.12.1 inside env). If that fixes, then the symlink sharing is the cause.
- Try using a torch wheel built for CUDA 12.2 (or rebuild from source) to match host driver. If that fixes, long-term solution: standardize on a single CUDA minor version for builds and host.
- Run gpustat and check for stale processes and memory fragmentation: sudo fuser -v /dev/nvidia* and nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY
- Test bumping environment variable for PyTorch caching: export PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1 (or set TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128) and see effect on allocation.
- Check container runtime (nvidia-container-toolkit) version; upgrade to latest if old.
- If dmesg still shows 'probe routine failed' after driver reinstall, collect /proc/driver/nvidia/version and full dmesg to escalate to infra.

Quick experiment commands to run (for whoever picks this up):
- On test node:
sudo reboot
# after boot
sudo systemctl status nvidia-persistenced
/usr/bin/gpustat -cp; nvidia-smi -L; nvidia-smi -q | head -n 40
# run container w/ explicit LD_LIBRARY_PATH to container cuda
docker run --gpus all --rm -e LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/conda/lib:/opt/conda/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/lib my-image:gpu-debug bash -c "python /app/inference/run_smoke.py"

- ldd check inside container for torch libs:
ldd /opt/conda/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/lib/libc10_cuda.so | grep -E 'cudart|cudnn|cublas' || true

- record kernel module state:
cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version || true
lsmod | grep nvidia || true

Notes to escalate with SRE if above doesn't fix:
- Attach full dmesg and the exact kernel module versions, nv-lsmod, and the binary versions for libcudart and libcudnn on both host and container.
- Include job id and timestamps so infra can check driver logs.

Potential long-term fixes/guardrails:
- Build and publish PyTorch wheels that match the host CUDA minor (standardize on 12.2 across infra) or move to container runtime that bundles CUDA runtime fully isolated (don’t use host /usr/local/cuda symlink).
- Add CI checks that validate container ldd of /site-packages/torch against expected /opt/cuda path.
- Add an inference runtime health-check that runs a small allocation test after container start and alerts on weird large reservations.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Why does a full host reboot help longer than container restart? (likely driver/kernel state) -> capture kernel module stack traces next time.
- Confirm whether cuDNN is needed by this workload; missing libcudnn in container might trigger fallback to host libs with mismatched ABI.
- Check whether we saw similar incidents across other nodes around the same time (correlate with driver updates / kernel updates).

References / past notes:
- See users/gpu-oom-debug-notes-asha-patel.json for similar OOM that turned out to be memory fragmentation with a fixed old nvidia-container-toolkit.
- Confluence: GPU OOM runbook (linked above).

Hand-off checklist for SRE/infra team:
- Collected: dmesg excerpt, nvidia-smi output, container ldd outputs, python memory_summary
- Ask SRE to: verify kernel modules, check for known driver regressions for 535.86.01, optionally re-provision a node with driver + cuda 12.1 or 12.2 consistently.
- Ask infra to hold off on node patching until we have stable reproduce steps (avoid mid-job driver upgrades).

Notes to self (short-term):
- If seeing this live: try container restart -> if still fails, escalate with timestamps and attach these logs.
- For next build: try to switch to torch wheel for CUDA 12.2 and avoid mounting host /usr/local/cuda inside container.

End of notes. Will update with new outputs if/when I re-run reproducer.
